title: COUNT(*) and COUNT(x) count null values differently
summary: COUNT(*) counts the result rows, COUNT(x) only counts the rows for which expression x is not NULL.
applies: SQLite query results and crossing dialect boundaries
detail: If LEFT JOIN does not match, the left row will still be retained. At this time, COUNT on the non-empty primary key on the right side will get 0, and COUNT(*) will get 1.
boundary: Duplicate values are still counted in COUNT(x); only explicit DISTINCT counts as distinct non-NULL values.
relevance: Check why the summary number returned by the web backend and the number of detailed rows differ by one.
